```json
{"claims":[{"claim_text":"Today's deficit, although unwelcome, is well within historical ranges.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"A deficit of 3.8 percent of GDP, as projected for this year, would be smaller than the deficits in nine of the last 25 years.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"A deficit of 3.8 percent of GDP is far below the peak deficit figure of 6 percent of GDP reached in 1983.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"This deficit is in line with what other industrialized nations are facing today.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The U.S. deficit matches the average deficit within the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The U.S. deficit is below the levels of France, Germany, and Japan.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Next year's projected deficit, at 2.7 percent of GDP, would be smaller than those in 14 of the last 25 years.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"As Republicans in Congress work with the President to restrain spending and strengthen economic growth, the federal deficit will fall to 1.5 percent of the nation's economic output in 2009.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"A federal deficit of 1.5 percent of the nation's economic output in 2009 is well below the 2.2 percent average of the last 40 years.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
```
